title: Platform Systems & Services — How-Tos, Dashboards, Runbooks, and Roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview:

This page consolidates the platform engineering artifacts for Redwood Inference: systems & services inventory, dashboards and alerting standards, operational runbooks, common how-tos, a short retrospective of recent incidents, and the platform roadmap for Q2 2026. Use this page as the canonical reference for on-call, new joiners, and cross-team coordination.

1) Systems & Services inventory (summary)

- api-gateway (service name: redwood-api-gw)
  - Owner: eng-platform / oncall: api-gateway-pagerduty
  - Primary function: edge ingress, routing, auth enforcement, rate-limiting
  - SLOs: availability 99.95% monthly, request error rate <0.1% (5xx), p99 latency <200 ms
  - Key downstreams: inference-router, auth-service, metrics-collector

- inference-router (service name: inference-router)
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime
  - Primary function: routing to model-serving pools (hosted/dedicated/private), model variant fallback
  - SLOs: availability 99.9%, request success rate >99.5%, p95 latency <300 ms for lightweight models
  - Notes: supports traffic shaping and smart routing policies. See kernel selection doc for perf profiles.

- model-cache (service name: kv-model-cache)
  - Owner: eng-serving-runtime
  - Primary function: prefix/KV caching for serving runtime
  - SLOs: cache hit rate target >=60% for steady workloads, eviction tail <5%

- telemetry-ingest (service name: metrics-collector)
  - Owner: eng-platform
  - Primary function: rollup of request traces, cost breakdowns, and real-time dashboards
  - SLOs: 99% of critical metrics available within 60s

2) Dashboards & Alerts (standards and key dashboards)

Standards (all dashboards):
- Every production service must have: Overview dashboard, Error-mode dashboard, Capacity & utilization dashboard, Cost breakdown dashboard (per-model, per-route).
- Dashboard naming convention: "Platform / <service> / <view>" (e.g., "Platform / inference-router / Overview").
- Panels must include owner and runbook link in panel description.

Key dashboards and recommended panels:
- Platform / api-gateway / Overview:
  - Global error rate (5xx, 4xx), requests per second, p50/p95/p99 latency, active connections, top 10 routes by RPS.
- Platform / inference-router / Health:
  - Request routing success, fallback count (per model variant), KV cache hit rate, queue length per model pool.
- Platform / model-cache / Capacity:
  - Memory usage by shard, eviction rate, hit ratio by route.

Alerting policy (owned by eng-sre + service owner):
- Critical alerts (PagerDuty P1): immediate paging to service owner and eng-sre
  - api-gateway: 5xx rate >0.5% for >5 minutes AND RPS > 50 (suppresses noisy low-traffic spikes)
  - inference-router: model-pool OOM/restart count >3 in 10m OR p95 latency >1000ms for 5m
  - telemetry-ingest: metrics backlog >30 minutes OR >5% ingestion errors for 10m
- Warning alerts (email + Slack):
  - cache hit rate <45% for 10m
  - cost spike: per-route token cost > 200% of 7-day rolling median for 15m

Alert ownership and escalation:
- PagerDuty service mapping: api-gateway -> PD service "api-gateway-prod"; inference-router -> "inference-router-prod"; metrics-collector -> "telemetry-prod".
- Escalation schedule: primary -> secondary (30m) -> oncall-manager (60m) -> SRE lead (90m).

3) Runbooks (templates + example: API Gateway high 5xx rate)

Runbook template (each runbook must include the sections below):
- Title
- Symptoms / detection (alerts that trigger this runbook)
- Owner / who to page
- Impact assessment checklist (what to check first)
- Immediate mitigation steps (quick fixes or fallbacks)
- Post-incident actions (rollout, rollback, postmortem link)
- Runbook test instructions (how to run periodically)

Example: "API Gateway — High 5xx Rate" runbook (short version)
1. Symptoms: PagerDuty alert "api-gateway 5xx-rate-critical" triggered. Error rate >0.5% for >5m while RPS >50.
2. Page: api-gateway-oncall (via PD). If unresolved for 15m, page eng-sre.
3. Impact assessment:
   - Check Overview dashboard: are errors concentrated on a single route?
   - Check deployment history: any recent release in last 30 minutes (CI/CD link: https://ci.redwood.internal/job/api-gw-deploys)
   - Check upstream latency: auth-service, inference-router.
4. Mitigation steps (ordered):
   a) If errors are route-specific: apply temporary traffic split to route-0 (fallback variant) using routing-api:
      - CLI: redwoodctl routing set-split --route <route> --percent 0.
   b) If a recent deployment caused errors: roll back to last stable deploy (CLI example):
      - redwoodctl deploy rollback --service api-gateway --to-release <tag>
   c) If auth-service failures present: add fallback allowlist for minimal auth for health-checking (follow security guidance in secure-sdlc).
5. Post-incident: create a retrospective PRD, tag incident number in commit messages, schedule follow-up with product if change in routing or quota policies required.

4) How-Tos (operational procedures)

A. Adding a new panel to Grafana (owner: eng-platform)
1. Open the dashboard: Grafana -> "Platform / <service> / Overview"
2. Click "Edit" -> "Add panel" -> choose data source "metrics-prometheus-prod"
3. Add a PromQL query (example for 5xx rate):
   - sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job=~\"api-gateway\", status=~\"5..\"}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job=~\"api-gateway\"}[5m]))
4. In the panel settings: set thresholds (warning 0.2%, critical 0.5%), add runbook link and owner in "Description"
5. Save with versioned message and notify #platform-alerting channel.

B. Creating a new alert rule (Prometheus Alertmanager)
1. Edit the alert rule file in git repo: infra-monitoring/alerts/api-gateway-rules.yaml
2. Add a rule block with summary, expr, for, labels (severity, team) and annotations (runbook)
3. Open PR, request review from eng-sre and service owner, merge to main.
4. Monitoring: alert should appear in Alertmanager within 2 minutes; test with alertmanagerctl silence/test.

C. Onboarding a new service to Platform monitoring
1. Create service entry in service-catalog.yaml (fields: name, owner, PD-service, slack-channel, runbook-link). Example:
   - name: new-vectorizer
     owner: eng-serving-runtime
     pagerduty: new-vectorizer-prod
     slack: #eng-serving-runtime
     runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/new-vectorizer-runbook
2. Add metrics instrumentation using standard libraries (see SDK: metrics-client v2)
3. Create dashboards and alert rules per standards above
4. Run a telemetry smoke test (send synthetic requests for 10 minutes) and verify dashboard panels

5) Retrospective (summary of recent incidents and follow-ups)

- Incident: "API gateway partial outage" (2026-01-14)
  - Root cause: rolling deploy with configuration drift in rate-limiting rules caused a subset of routes to return 503s under specific header combinations.
  - Mitigation: rollback, temporary global-ratelimit relax, and applied staged rollout policy.
  - Action items: tighten deploy gating (feature flags + pre-deploy synthetic tests), add canary traffic rule for rate-limit config changes, add test case to regression suite.
  - Owner: eng-platform (Ava Martinez), due: 2026-03-14 (status: completed).

- Incident: "Inference-router latency spike" (2025-12-02)
  - Root cause: KV cache eviction storm during model snapshot refresh.
  - Mitigation: increased cache capacity, added jitter to snapshot refresh, and tuned eviction policy.
  - Action items: implement backpressure on snapshot refresh and improve monitoring for cache churn. Owner: eng-serving-runtime (Sofia Patel).

6) Roadmap (Q2 2026 priorities)

Objectives:
- Improve platform reliability & operability:
  - Deliver 'deploy-gate' (canary + synthetic testing) — target ship: 2026-04-15 (owner: eng-platform)
  - Add runbook test harness & scheduled runbook drills — target 2026-05-01 (owner: eng-sre)
- Cost & performance optimizations:
  - Per-route cost attribution (dashboard + daily alerts for cost anomalies) — target 2026-04-30 (owner: eng-platform + finance)
  - Auto-suggest batching/quantization profiles for heavy routes (prototype) — target 2026-06-15 (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Observability & tooling:
  - High-cardinality trace sampling improvements and trace-to-metric mapping — target 2026-05-20 (owner: eng-platform)

Roadmap timeline (high level):
- April: deploy-gate rollout + canary configuration UI
- May: runbook drill framework + trace sampling improvements
- June: cost attribution dashboards + batching suggestion prototype

7) Team wiki & onboarding links
- Platform team wiki: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-team-wiki-and-runbooks-2026
- Monitoring repo: git@internal:redwood/infra-monitoring.git (owner: eng-sre)
- CI/CD deploys: https://ci.redwood.internal (internal access required)
- Runbook examples: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-operations-playbook-2026

8) Ownership, SLAs, and contacts
- Platform oncall rotation: https://pagerduty.com/redwood/schedules/platform (primary and secondary)
- SLO review cadence: quarterly; SLO owners must produce an SLO report 7 days before each review.
- Contact matrix:
  - eng-platform pager: #eng-platform-oncall (Slack)
  - eng-sre lead: li.wei@redwood.ai
  - incident commander escalation: oncall-manager@redwood.ai

Appendix (snippets & configs)
- Example alert rule (YAML):
  - alert: APIGatewayHigh5xxRate
    expr: |
      sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job=~\"api-gateway\", status=~\"5..\"}[5m]))
      / sum(rate(http_server_requests_total{job=~\"api-gateway\"}[5m])) > 0.005
    for: 5m
    labels:
      severity: critical
      team: eng-platform
    annotations:
      summary: "api-gateway 5xx rate >0.5% for 5m"
      runbook: "/confluence/eng-platform/api-gateway-high-5xx-runbook"

- CLI: routing split example:
  redwoodctl routing set-split --route user-vectorize-v1 --percent 0 --reason "mitigation: redirect to fallback"

Testing & compliance
- Runbook drills: quarterly table-top + one live drill per year. Drill outcomes recorded in /confluence/eng-platform/runbook-drills-2026.
- Audit: monitoring changes (alerts/dashboards) are retained via Git history and audited quarterly for drift.

If anything on this page is out of date or missing, please file an edit request and @mention the owner in the first paragraph.
